verdict.rationale: NRQL is documented as a SQL-like language for querying New Relic data to answer ad-hoc troubleshooting questions, and the logs UI lets you filter by specific attributes. That implies ad-hoc filtering, but nothing explicitly documents grouping by high-cardinality fields or doing so without pre-aggregation or indexes. A community report of 'metric names exploding' points to cardinality friction, at least in the metric data model. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of GROUP BY/FACET on high-cardinality attributes such as user or request ID, evidence that no pre-aggregation or index definition is required, documented cardinality limits, and independent hands-on corroboration.
